newsitem.title: USA: Communications Systems sees benefit from unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Communications Systems sees benefit from unit sale.

text.p: Communications Systems Inc on Wednesday said the recently announced pending sale of its Zercom Inc contract manufacturing subsidiary will significantly strengthen the company's financial ratios and profit margins.
It said the sale also will allow Communications Systems to focus exclusively on its global telecommunications operations.
The company on October 1 said it signed a definitive agreement under which Nortech Systems Inc, an electronic contract manufacturer, will acquire assets of Zercom.
The transaction is expected to close on October 31. Terms of the pending divestiture include a significant down payment to the company plus a five-year note secured by the unit's assets.

Communications Systems president Curtis Sampson said Zercom historically has generated gross margins in the range of 12 to 14 percent compared with the company's telecommunications margins in excess of 30 percent.
He said the company's financial ratios, including returns on sales, equity and assets, also will improve materially in the absence of the contract manufacturing operations.

The enhancements in profit margins and financial ratios will be seen in the company's financial statements starting in the 1996 third quarter, the company said. Its historic financial statements, including those for this year's first and second quarters, will be restated to reflect the divestiture.

In the absence of Zercom, the company would have reported consolidated net sales of $32.2 million in the first half of 1996 compared with the $41 million reported for the period. Without Zercom, consolidated net income would have been $3.7 million or $0.39 per share in this year's first half versus the $3.3 million or $0.36 per share that was reported.
